thread:
Tessa Morgan: Quick review request for Suggestions (beta) empty states + onboarding tooltip copy. Main open question: when we don’t have enough telemetry/signal, do we show “Insufficient data” cards, or hide suggestions entirely? I’m leaning show, but need alignment before I lock copy.

Alicia Perez: +1 to deciding today. In the mocks I dropped into Figma yesterday, I used a “No suggestions yet” empty state + secondary line “We need at least 24h of recent traffic to estimate savings.” Concern is we’ll get “nothing here” confusion if it’s just blank.

Kenji Nakamura: I’m worried “Insufficient data” reads like a bug. Especially if they *do* have traffic but telemetry freshness is behind. If we show “insufficient data” we need a very clear “what we’re missing” + what they can do. Otherwise support will hate us.

Marissa Cole: Product POV: we should not hide it entirely. Beta goal is trust + explainability. If we hide, users assume the feature is broken / not enabled. A visible empty state gives a place for a tooltip + docs link.

Svetlana Orlov: From design system angle, we already have an “EmptyState” pattern with icon + title + body + CTA. We can also do an “InfoBanner” at top when filters result in 0 rows. But I’d avoid mixing “0 suggestions” and “can’t compute suggestions” without distinct language.

Dylan Brooks: Eng note: backend is going to return `status=NO_DATA` vs `status=OK` (and maybe `status=STALE_BASELINE` later). If we hide everything, we lose ability to distinguish those states. Also we *need* a place to tell them why they’re not seeing anything.

Tessa Morgan: Totally. The debate is mainly: list view should show placeholder rows with reason (“insufficient data”), OR a single empty state card. I’m not in favor of placeholder rows; feels noisy.

Alicia Perez: Agree no placeholder rows. One empty state card for the whole view is better.

Kenji Nakamura: If we do a single empty state, can we avoid the phrase “insufficient data” in the title? Maybe title is “No suggestions available yet” and body explains “We don’t have enough recent telemetry to estimate savings.” Title reads less accusatory.

Marissa Cole: That works. But we should still use the “data” word somewhere so it’s clear it’s not just “we didn’t find anything.”

Svetlana Orlov: Copy suggestion:
- Title: “No suggestions yet”
- Body: “We need recent usage telemetry to generate cost and latency estimates. Check again after more traffic or verify telemetry is enabled.”
Then a small link: “How suggestions work” / “Telemetry requirements”.

Tessa Morgan: What about cases where telemetry exists but doesn’t meet thresholds (ex: low volume)? Do we treat that the same as telemetry missing?

Dylan Brooks: Backend will send reason codes. Right now we have (draft) `NO_TRAFFIC`, `NO_TELEMETRY`, `TELEMETRY_STALE`, `INCOMPATIBLE_ROUTE` (e.g., no streaming metrics). But v1 might just bucket as `NO_DATA`.

Alicia Perez: Can we make body copy dynamic based on reason code? Even if title stays “No suggestions yet.”

Dylan Brooks: Yes, we can do a mapping table in UI. I’d prefer that over shoving all caveats into one paragraph.

Kenji Nakamura: If we do dynamic body copy, we should be careful with “verify telemetry is enabled” because that sounds like an action they can control when sometimes it’s “not enough traffic.”

George Mbatha: Jumping in with UX research lens: in early feedback sessions, users interpret “No suggestions” as “the system thinks I’m already optimized.” When they later see “estimated savings” elsewhere, it creates distrust. So we should explicitly call out the constraint (“not enough data to compute”).

Tessa Morgan: Great point. So: title “No suggestions yet” + first sentence “We don’t have enough recent data to estimate savings for this workspace.”

Marissa Cole: + docs link. Also consider Support’s expected FAQ: “Why don’t I see Suggestions?” So the empty state should basically answer that.

Svetlana Orlov: Tooltip copy question: Where is tooltip anchored? On the page header (“Suggestions”) or on the empty state itself?

Alicia Perez: I had it as an onboarding tooltip next to the header in the first-time experience (“Suggestions analyzes your traffic and proposes batching/caching changes”). But for empty state, a tooltip feels weird; a link in-body is better.

Kenji Nakamura: +1. Tooltips should be additive, not required to understand empty states.

Tessa Morgan: Ok. Tooltip: only for first-time entry, not specifically empty state. Empty state gets CTA link.

Dylan Brooks: Implementation note: we can gate the onboarding tooltip behind `suggestions_beta` and also behind “firstSeenSuggestionsView” local storage. But for enterprise users who share accounts, local storage isn’t reliable.

Marissa Cole: For beta, that’s fine. We can always show “Learn how this works” link in the header too.

Alicia Perez: Another nuance: filters. If they filter to a model/region with no suggestions, that should say “No results for these filters” not “No suggestions yet.”

Svetlana Orlov: Yes please. Separate states:
1) Global empty state (no data / no suggestions computed)
2) Empty results state (filters yield 0)
We have both patterns.

Kenji Nakamura: On the “hide suggestions vs show insufficient data” debate — I’m ok showing, as long as we don’t use the scary red error tone. It should be neutral info.

Tessa Morgan: Agreed. Visual language: info icon, not warning. No red.

George Mbatha: Wording “insufficient telemetry” tested poorly in other products. It reads like instrumentation failure. Users also don’t know what “telemetry” is. Recommend “usage data” in primary copy; “telemetry” can be in the docs.

Alicia Perez: +1. “Usage data” feels more human.

Marissa Cole: Works for PLG. For enterprise, they may be familiar with telemetry but still fine.

Tessa Morgan: Draft copy v2:
- Title: “No suggestions yet”
- Body (default): “We don’t have enough recent usage data to estimate savings. Suggestions typically appear after ~24 hours of steady traffic.”
- Link: “Learn what data Suggestions uses”
- Secondary (if telemetry stale): “We haven’t received fresh usage data recently. If this persists, contact Support.”
Thoughts?

Kenji Nakamura: “steady traffic” could be interpreted as “high volume.” Maybe “after ~24 hours of traffic” without “steady”.

Alicia Perez: Agree. Also don’t promise 24h; maybe “often” / “typically”.

Svetlana Orlov: Suggest:
“Suggestions typically appear after we’ve observed enough traffic (often within 24 hours).”

Dylan Brooks: +1 on not hard promising 24h. Backend thresholds depend on volume.

Marissa Cole: Add a sentence about “If you just enabled Suggestions, it may take time to populate.” That handles beta enablement confusion.

Tessa Morgan: Ok updated:
“Suggestions typically appear after we’ve observed enough traffic (often within 24 hours). If you just enabled Suggestions, it may take some time to populate.”

George Mbatha: That’s good. One more: in the empty state, can we mention “Check filters”? People get stuck filtering to a route with no traffic.

Alicia Perez: Maybe only in the filter-empty state. Otherwise it’s too much.

Kenji Nakamura: Agree. Separate.

Tessa Morgan: Decision check:
- We DO show an empty state (not hide the feature)
- Avoid “insufficient data” as a headline; use “No suggestions yet”
- Use “usage data” instead of “telemetry” in UI
- Different empty states for: (a) no data / can’t compute, (b) filter yields no results
Everyone ok?

Marissa Cole: ✅

Dylan Brooks: ✅ (and we’ll map reason codes to body copy)

Alicia Perez: ✅

Kenji Nakamura: ✅

Svetlana Orlov: ✅ I’ll point you to the EmptyState component props + spacing tokens.

George Mbatha: ✅

Tessa Morgan: Great. I’ll update the copy doc + Figma frames today and ping #support with the final strings for FAQ alignment. :thumbsup:

(reactions) Kenji Nakamura added :white_check_mark:
